Check every tutorial in a package

Source: R/check_tutorials.R
check_tutorials.Rd

The one call a content package's tests need. Finds every tutorial the package ships (with available_tutorials(), so a package loaded with pkgload::load_all() is checked from its source tree), runs check_tutorial()'s static checks on each, renders each with render_tutorials(), and checks the rendered page: that its download file will say which package, version and tutorial it is a submission for (see download_answers_button()). Problems from every stage come back in one data frame, and by default the function stops if any is an error.

Usage

check_tutorials(
  package = NULL,
  render = TRUE,
  skip = NULL,
  output_dir = tempfile("learnr2-check-"),
  quiet = TRUE,
  error = TRUE
)

Arguments

package

Name of the package whose tutorials to check. NULL, the default, checks every installed package that has tutorials, plus any loaded with pkgload::load_all(); a content package's own test passes its name.

render

Render each tutorial too? TRUE by default. Rendering needs the Quarto command line tool and takes a few seconds per tutorial; pass !is.null(quarto::quarto_path()) to skip it where Quarto is missing.

skip

Check names to leave out, as for check_tutorial(). Two more names apply here: "render" (the render itself) and "submission" (the rendered page's download header).

output_dir

Where to render, as for render_tutorials().

quiet

Passed to render_tutorials().

error

If TRUE (the default), stop listing every error-level problem, after a warning for the warning-level ones. If FALSE, just return them.

Value

A data frame of problems with columns path, check, severity and message, invisibly; zero rows when everything passed.

In a content package's tests

test_that("every tutorial passes learnr2's checks", {
  skip_on_cran()
  expect_no_error(learnr2::check_tutorials(
    "my.tutorials", render = !is.null(quarto::quarto_path())
  ))
})

Examples

# learnr2's own tutorials, static checks only (rendering needs Quarto).
problems <- check_tutorials("learnr2", render = FALSE, error = FALSE)
problems[, c("check", "message")]
